name: Titus
summary: A Greek believer who travelled with Paul and was his trusted partner. Paul sent him to the Corinthians, was comforted by his coming, and left him in Crete to set things in order and appoint elders.

key_moments.title: Goes Up to Jerusalem with Paul
key_moments.description: Paul took Titus with him and Barnabas when he went up to Jerusalem. Though Titus was a Greek, he was not forced to be circumcised.

key_moments.title: Comforts Paul in Macedonia
key_moments.description: When Paul came into Macedonia, troubled on all sides, God comforted him when Titus arrived. Titus brought news of the Corinthians' longing and care for Paul, which made him rejoice even more.

key_moments.title: Sent to the Corinthians
key_moments.description: God gave Titus the same deep care for the Corinthians that Paul had, and he gladly went to them on his own. Paul called him his partner and fellow helper.

key_moments.title: Left in Crete
key_moments.description: Paul wrote to Titus as his own son in the faith they shared. He had left Titus in Crete to set right what was lacking and to appoint elders in each city.
